scope: One complete aboveground shaft surface structure at the eastern of the three northern anonymous shaft points. Nearby free-standing buildings, conveyors, other shafts and plant equipment remain separate.
appearanceSources: Existing published Qualla NASA ISS038-E-29810 first
observation: Both existing NASA originals show a compact pale industrial mass with darker tall surface structure and an elongated shadow in the northern east shaft region. Surrounding road bends and the relative arrangement of the three northern shaft regions support a broad association with the original shaft point. The images are too coarse for measured footprint, section, exact steel topology or named shaft identification.
correspondence: Broad two-view and independent numerical-point/road-context inference, not surveyed image registration. Earlier pond-control extrapolation has visible local displacement; it is not used to move the original shaft point or to trace model dimensions.
chosenBody: Estimated open tapered steel shaft surface support, two inclined backstays, closed upper machinery housing, central guide structure, small lower collar enclosure, independent concrete support pads and estimated access platforms. This is a conservative original medium-fi interpretation of the tall surface form; its headgear topology and equipment identity are not verified.
unmeasured: aboveground structural type and exact topology
